intent_summary: The reusable anomaly-detection Skill guides an agent through local Anomalyzer analysis and a concise explanation grounded in structured evidence.

criteria.criterion: The Skill directs analysis through the installed Anomalyzer CLI, with executable fallback paths and structured JSON output, rather than a newly invented detector.
criteria.notes: Executable resolution and JSON commands are explicit. Manual conversion and spike CLI runs use the installed numerical engine.

criteria.criterion: The Skill instructs callers to preserve missing data, select one entity and unit, and explicitly declare compatible sources for related-metric analysis.
criteria.notes: Instructions preserve scope, units, missingness, declared relationships, and exact alignment; existing runtime checks establish these prerequisites.

criteria.criterion: The default response instructions lead with changes and observed-versus-expected values, then explain readiness, evidence maturity, overlapping findings, and material limitations without inventing confidence percentages or causes.
criteria.notes: The supplied instructions lead with plain-language changes and then qualify maturity/readiness/overlap. This establishes instructional content, not measured agent compliance.

criteria.criterion: The Skill describes MCP analyze, list_findings, and get_evidence as an optional evidence workflow and makes session lifetime, read-only access, and caller-owned notification and action delivery explicit.
criteria.notes: The documented three-tool workflow matches executed conversion drilldown, with session-only run IDs and explicit read-only/caller-owned delivery limits.

verification_evidence: Primary Codex agent re-inspected declared implementation references and criterion evidence in the current session after the outcome-title and deliverable-lane refactor.
Executed and inspected CLI examples, time preparation, policy replay, open-day monitoring, and MCP conversion evidence drilldown; .capabilities/reviews/deliverable-lanes/manual-checks.json.
Skill criteria covering agent instructions are supported by the written guidance and demonstrated tool workflow; cross-host agent compliance and real-world detection accuracy are not asserted.
